Authorization is now genuinely two axes: a stored **`users.role`** (`admin | member | viewer`) beside the per-suite `view/edit/admin/owner` ladder, both enforced on REST and MCP, both resolving **per request** — so a demotion lands on the target's next call, *including calls made with PATs they already hold*, with no token to revoke. `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` demotes to a **bootstrap seed + lockout break-glass** that only ever grants. **This closes gap G-e and the standing hole where any authenticated user — even one holding a single `view` share — could delete or re-credential the connection every suite in the workspace ran on** (⚠️ breaking for Members who managed connections; promote before upgrading, CHANGELOG carries the note). Roles are managed in **Admin → Members** behind a **last-admin guard that counts stored-role admins only** (an allowlist-resolved admin can vanish with the next deploy) under `FOR UPDATE`, with a structured audit line per change — the durable audit *table* stays ADR 0020's deferred #310.

input.old_string: **Unplanned, user-directed, shipped 2026-08-16 — the ADR [0033](docs/adr/0033-workspace-roles-rbac.md) workspace-roles (RBAC) track
input.new_string:
**Shipped 2026-08-17 — the MCP Tier-1 tool expansion (Theme 13, [#529](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/529), W7 stretch), taking `/mcp` from 8 tools to 19:** five PRs ([#1413](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1413)–[#1417](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1417)) adding the whole Tier-1 read-only set — checks (`list_checks`/`get_check`/`get_check_history`), runs (`list_runs`/`get_run_results`), ops/config (`list_connections`/`list_schedules`/`list_trigger_bindings`/`get_notification_config`), and aggregates (`get_suite_performance`/`export_suite`). Every one is a thin service-layer wrapper, so **no new authz was written**: `require_permission` already composes the ADR-0027 per-suite ladder with the ADR-0033 Viewer clamp, and the #741 exact-set tripwire forced each new tool to be enumerated with its gating rationale. The deliberate exclusions hold — no connection create/update/reauth, because a credential must never transit an LLM.

**The four `/code-review` passes returned 19 findings, and almost none were crashes — they were *honesty* defects, which is the failure mode this surface has and the REST API does not.** The same shape recurred six times: a value that is literally true and misleading to a reader with no UI around it. An expired snooze returned raw reads as active suppression on the one question ("why was there no alert?") where a wrong answer is most confident. A mid-run suite's partial outcome (`3/3, worst_severity: null`) is precisely the tool's own definition of "nothing failed", asserted about a run that has barely started — the REST runs table survives it only because a "running" badge sits beside the numbers; **an LLM has no badge, it has whatever fields it is handed**. `consecutive_run_failures: 0` renders *unknown* as a fact. A null `credential_expires_at` conflated "no readable lifetime" with "never looked". `has_email_recipients` was derived from `EMAIL_TO` while delivery also needs the SMTP transport. And `get_notification_config` reported only the per-suite webhook, so the commonest deployment shape — one workspace webhook, no overrides — answered "who gets told when orders fails?" with **nobody**. docs(mcp): reconcile every "8 tools" claim with the 19-tool surface (#529)

The Tier-1 expansion took `/mcp` from 8 tools to 19 and left the count stale in
a dozen places — README, both CLAUDE.md tech-stack tables and the `.mcp.json`
appendix, the mcp-setup tool table, feature-matrix, glossary, features,
runbook-faq, deployment-parity, and two comments inside `backend/app/mcp`
itself.

- **`docs/mcp-setup.md`** gets the real work: the flat 8-row table becomes five
  grouped sections (suites & results, checks, runs & profiling, connections &
  orchestration, scheduling & alerting), each description taken from the tool's
  own docstring rather than restated. It also says plainly that 17 of the 19 are
  read-only and only `trigger_suite_run` / `create_check` change anything.
- **ADR 0008** is amended, not rewritten: the Week-7 decision record stands as
  written, and an appended section documents the expansion, that the authz model
  is unchanged (thin wrapper + `require_permission`, so ADR 0027 sharing and the
  ADR 0033 Viewer clamp apply to the new tools for free), and the three standing
  exclusions — connections metadata-only, notification presence-only, and no
  connection-write tool at all, because a credential must never transit an LLM.
- **Theme 13** in the post-v1 roadmap marks Tier 1 delivered; **Tier 2 stays
  open**, and #529 stays open with it.

Historical records were deliberately left alone: the v1.0.0 changelog entry,
`docs/progress-v1.md`, the retro, the v1 roadmap, and the CLAUDE.md §13
narrative of past incidents all describe what was true when written.

Beyond the unit tests, the surface was exercised **through the real MCP
protocol** (in-memory FastMCP client against Postgres): 19 tools registered,
every one carrying a description and a valid JSON-Schema input; the advertised
bounds enforced by the protocol layer, not just the function body; and all 11
new tools called for real, confirming `Decimal` thresholds and metrics survive
serialization — the layer a direct Python call bypasses entirely.
EOF
)" && git push -u origin docs/mcp-tier1-expansion 2>&1|tail -1
